rules: An identifier is opaque: it is generated once, never reused, never re-issued after correction and never parsed to recover business meaning.
The ULID body must not be decoded by domain or consumer logic to derive creation time, ownership, ordering or any other business attribute.

A filesystem path, directory name, uploaded file name, S3 object key, URL, display ordinal such as F-014, human sheet or document number and any content checksum are addresses, presentation values or verification values; none of them is an identity and none may be used as a foreign key.
An identifier is stable for the lifetime of its entity. Correcting data creates a new entity with a new identifier; it never rewrites an existing one.
Identifiers carry no secret. They are safe to log, to place in error envelope details and to return to an authorized caller.
Prefixes are globally unique across this catalog; a new entity requires a new catalog entry and a new prefix.
Cross-entity references use the referenced identifier verbatim. No composite, derived, encoded or human-readable compound key is defined by this contract.

Suffix -uid marks the workspace/semantic identities carried over from 1.0.0-draft.0 and -id marks every other identity. The suffix is retained for consumer stability only; it is not a type discriminator and grants no different guarantee.

NormDocument and NormParagraph are immutable public entities inside NormsSnapshot and carry their own opaque identifiers. A rebuildable retrieval chunk, its ordinal and its chunking profile are projections and have no public entity identity.

The canonical name of the execution authority capability is execution_token. fencing_token and authority_token are legacy or cross-lane evidence names only; no target field, payload key, database column or API parameter defined against this contract carries them.

The canonical version key of every catalog in this family is contract_version, a string semver or draft version. $schema stays the JSON Schema dialect and $id stays schema identity; neither is a contract version.

portal_block_id.origin: the portal that produced the bundle; carried verbatim from the _blocks.json block list
portal_block_id.scope: one version_uid: the pair (version_uid, portal_block_id) addresses a block, and the same value in two versions names two unrelated rows
rules: Never generated, reissued or parsed by this product: the 32 hexadecimal digits carry no meaning here.
Not an entry of identifiers: the product's identities are prefix_ULID values it mints, and this one is neither.
Only addressed under /versions/{version_uid}/portal-blocks. A bare portal_block_id authorizes nothing and names nothing.

distinct_identities.name: finding_identity
distinct_identities.rule: finding_uid is the durable semantic issue identity that carries expert history across reruns. finding_observation_id is immutable evidence emitted by exactly one run_id. A rerun creates new observations and never rewrites or removes earlier ones. When the versioned matching policy cannot justify carryover it allocates a new finding_uid instead of reusing one.

distinct_identities.name: execution_identity
distinct_identities.rule: AuditRun is the business request and result history, Job is the durable schedulable work item, Attempt is one concrete leased execution. None substitutes for another, none is derived from another and none may be reconstructed from project_uid, version_uid or a worker task handle.

distinct_identities.name: decision_identity
distinct_identities.rule: Every expert verdict, correction and revocation allocates a new decision_id and appends a new immutable event. A decision_id is never reused, updated in place or removed; the current verdict is a rebuildable projection over the event stream.

distinct_identities.name: input_identity
distinct_identities.rule: version_uid is the immutable published input state, blob_id is durable content bytes with checksum metadata and import_id is the operation that produced them. A project folder, an upload batch name or an S3 key is none of these.

distinct_identities.name: normative_corpus_identity
distinct_identities.rule: NormsSnapshot identifies one immutable corpus state, NormDocument one immutable member document and NormParagraph one immutable canonical paragraph. Each is allocated independently and never derived from content or from another identity. Retrieval chunks are rebuildable projections over canonical paragraphs and have no public entity identity. NormRetrievalSet identifies a verified, snapshot-bound set and catalogue; its map digest, content key and artifact checksums are attributes, never substitutes for nrs_ identity.

distinct_identities.name: account_identity
distinct_identities.rule: A RegistrationRequest is the history of one application and a User is the account an approval creates; neither substitutes for the other. Approval allocates a new user_uid and records it on the request, a rejected request creates no account, and purging an account never removes the request that created it. A login (the normalised e-mail address) is unique only among active accounts and pending requests, can be held again after an account is archived or purged, and is therefore never an identity or a foreign key.

distinct_identities.name: custody_identity
distinct_identities.rule: A NormCustodyAdmission is one custody intent with its outbox row; a NormCustodyBinding is the one published relation a confirmed admission becomes, binding a role, a target and an opaque anchor to a Blob. The Blob is content-derived and shared: equal verified bytes reuse one blob_id under any number of bindings and roles, and a failed admission is rejected without ever rejecting the shared Blob. Neither custody identity is derived from the blob_id, the declared SHA-256, the anchor, the target or a file name, and none of those is a custody identity or a foreign key in its place.
distinct_identities.authority: R-76 owner ruling 2026-10-09 and R-104 owner ruling 2026-10-12

distinct_identities.name: repair_call_identity
distinct_identities.rule: A NormRepairCall is one paid provider try of the corpus repair run, and its idempotency scope is its own norm_repair_call_id. A retry is a new try with a new identity and the next attempt number; an outcome_unknown try is never re-paid. The block anchor, crop SHA-256 and request SHA-256 are verification and lookup values, never the identity.

distinct_identities.name: optimisation_identity
distinct_identities.rule: PriceList identifies one immutable upload of a project's price list (a revision); PriceListPosition one parsed position of exactly one PriceList; VendorList one immutable revision of a section's vendor list, global or of one project. Each is allocated independently. A revision number, a source row number, the uploaded file name, the file's checksum and a section code are attributes and display values, never substitutes for these identities; correcting a price list or a vendor list creates a new revision with a new identity.
distinct_identities.authority: W60-PRICE-LIST-01; ROADMAP-TO-BETA.md section 10.1 A-3 to A-5

distinct_identities.name: optimisation_proposal_identity
distinct_identities.rule: OptimisationPass identifies one immutable pass over the current AR version of one document set, pinned to its published run, price-list revision and vendor-list revision; OptimisationProposal one deterministic proposal of exactly one OptimisationPass; ProposalDecision one appended expert decision on exactly one OptimisationProposal. Each is allocated independently and none is a finding or an ExpertDecision: a proposal is a separate entity beside findings with its own decisions, counts and export. A proposal's ordinal, a decision's seq, a specification row's provenance key and a position's row number are display or ordering values, never substitutes for these identities; a corrected pass is a new OptimisationPass.
distinct_identities.authority: W60-OPT-PROPOSALS-01; ROADMAP-TO-BETA.md section 10.1 A-2 to A-5

distinct_identities.name: executor_connection_identity
distinct_identities.rule: ExecutorConnection identifies where a process sends model work, for its whole life; ExecutorConnectionRevision one immutable set of its non-secret settings, so a changed address is a new revision and never an edit; ExecutorSecret one sealed secret of exactly one connection and purpose, replaced by a new row and never rewritten; ExecutorProbe one probe of a revision; ExecutorRouteEvent one appended change of the route for a kind of model work. Each is allocated independently. A host name, an address, a model name, a display name or a secret's last four characters is an attribute and never an identity, and a secret's identity is part of the associated data its ciphertext is sealed under.

distinct_identities.name: executor_task_identity
distinct_identities.rule: ExecutorRunnerToken identifies one credential a remote runner presents to the pull channel of exactly one connection, for its whole life; ExecutorTask one unit of model work handed to a runner, tied to the run, Attempt and model call that wait for it. Each is allocated independently. The token's secret value, its shown prefix, its hash and a task's position in a queue are attributes and never identities: the value is shown once and only its one-way hash is stored, so the identity is what an administrator addresses to revoke it.

distinct_identities.name: comparison_foundation_identity
distinct_identities.rule: ComparisonUpload identifies one upload batch of plain PDFs for comparison; ComparisonUploadSet one proposed document set of it (the original's batch item) and ComparisonUploadFile one declared file, whose display name is a hint and whose declared SHA-256 and size are verification values; ComparisonVersionOrder one revision of the order in which the versions of a document set are compared and never changes a version's ordinal; ComparisonPageProfile the raw profile of one page of one version, content-keyed (a ULID id and a unique digest column, the digest never a foreign key); ComparisonWork one item of the comparison-local durable queue and ComparisonWorkAttempt one leased execution of it, neither a Job nor an Attempt (a Job is a Run in the schema); ComparisonModelCall one row of the comparison spend journal, not a ModelCallRecord. Each is allocated independently and never parsed.

distinct_identities.name: comparison_core_identity
distinct_identities.rule: ComparisonMatrix identifies one algorithmic build of the matrix of a document set (the effective matrix is a read model over a build, accepted AI links and manual edits) and ComparisonMatrixEdit one event of the append-only manual edit history, whose pages are a version and a coordinate in it; a migrated 0035 approval keeps its cmp_ and sln_ ids in provenance and is not identified by them; ComparisonAiLink one accepted AI link, never an expert act; ComparisonSeries one series of adjacent transitions for one version order, ComparisonTransition one adjacent pair of versions of it (two version identities, never an ordinal) and ComparisonSheetPair one row of a transition that points at a result; ComparisonSheetPairResult the content-keyed result of comparing two pages (a ULID id and a unique digest column that includes the project; the digest is never a foreign key), shared by pairs of equal content within a project. Each is allocated independently and never parsed.

correlation_id.purpose: Correlates one externally visible request or command with its diagnostic logs, durable audit events and background work.
correlation_id.origin: assigned by the edge when the caller does not supply one
rules: Present in every error envelope so an operator can locate the full diagnostic record without the response carrying unsafe content.
Never used as a foreign key, never authorizes anything and never encodes subject, tenant or path information.
The events contract family declares its own correlation and causation fields; divergence in format is an integrator mismatch, not a domain-local fork.

idempotency_key.scope: command type plus authorized subject plus target aggregate
rules: The same key with the same payload fingerprint replays the recorded outcome and creates no second aggregate, version, run, attempt or decision.
The same key with a different payload fingerprint is a conflict (idempotency_key_reuse) and creates or changes nothing.
A key is never interpreted as, converted into or stored as a system identifier, and never appears in an error envelope.

payload_fingerprint.definition: sha256 over the RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme serialization of the command payload, taken after the payload validated against its declared command schema and after declared defaults were applied, and excluding transport headers and the idempotency key itself.
payload_fingerprint.purpose: Distinguishes an idempotent repeat from a same-key, different-payload conflict.

excluded: request framing, transfer encoding and any other envelope-level metadata
rules: The payload is validated against its declared command schema and default-normalized before it is canonicalized. An invalid payload is validation_failed and is never fingerprinted, so a malformed request can never take an idempotency key hostage.

Canonicalization is RFC 8785 JCS over that normalized payload and the fingerprint is the sha256 digest of its UTF-8 bytes. No provider defines a second canonical form and no provider falls back to another one.

Transport headers and the idempotency key itself are excluded from the fingerprint input, so two requests that differ only in transport framing produce the same fingerprint and replay instead of conflicting.
The fingerprint is a comparison value only: it is never an identity, never a foreign key, never parsed for meaning and never returned in an error envelope.
Both sides compute the fingerprint from the same normalized payload; a provider never fingerprints raw transport bytes.

execution_token.purpose: Proves that the bearer is the current authorized executor of a Job and its current Attempt at the instant of a write.
rules: execution_token is the only field name this contract declares for the execution authority capability. fencing_token and authority_token are legacy or cross-lane evidence names; a target field, payload key, database column or API parameter never carries them.

The issuing control plane allocates exactly one current token per job_id and supersedes the previous one when a new Attempt is created; a superseded token is permanently rejected and can never become current again.

The token is opaque and equality-only. Every other party, including engines and workers, compares it for exact equality and never parses, orders, ranges, increments, derives or uses it as a lookup key.

Fencing is a property of behavior, not of the value or of the field name: it holds because a superseded token can never publish again. This contract promises no monotonic number, no ordering and no comparability, and a consumer must not assume any.
Verified inside the same transaction that performs the guarded write; a check performed earlier in the request is not sufficient.
Never persisted as an entity identity and never accepted in place of attempt_id.

Secret-class value: never logged, never placed in an error message or details object and never returned to an unauthorized caller. execution_token, fencing_token and authority_token are all forbidden detail keys in the error catalog.
Its transport representation is declared by the execution/analysis contract family; this contract does not fix it.

lease.purpose: Time-bounded grant of execution authority to one Worker for one Attempt, kept alive by heartbeat.
rules: The lease record has identity; the execution token it carries is a capability and is not the lease identity.
Lease expiry returns the Job to queued, marks the Attempt lost and removes publication authority from that Attempt.
lease.open_question: Deferred as OQ-02: lease duration, heartbeat interval and grace window are operational values. They are decided by the jobs/operations slot no later than the first task that implements an execution lease (W4-JOB-01, durable stage state and bounded retry/resume). No numeric value is invented here and no lease implementation may proceed without that decision.

open_owner_decisions.statement: Expert correction and revocation append a new decision event with a new decision_id, decision history is neither deleted nor overwritten, and projections are recomputed from the event stream. The legacy overwrite and delete behavior recorded in EX-02 is not adopted.
open_owner_decisions.modification: Revocation moves the current projection for the affected finding to pending. The projection never restores an earlier superseded verdict automatically; a verdict after a revocation exists only where an authorized expert appended a new decision event. This modification also resolves OQ-03.

open_owner_decisions.statement: AuditRun, Job and Attempt are three distinct entities with separate identities, current-attempt authority is mandatory and a stale or superseded Attempt cannot publish. The execution authority capability is not an entity identity and not a path.
open_owner_decisions.modification: The AuditRun creation rule is fixed. A new AuditRun is created when a top-level audit or re-audit command is accepted for a frozen set of inputs and configurations. A repeat with the same idempotency key and the same payload returns the existing Run. Changed inputs, an explicit re-audit, or a repeat of a terminal Run create a new Run. Retry, resume, restart and worker failover create no Run and no Job: the Job stays the same and a new Attempt is created. A terminal Run is never reopened.

open_owner_decisions.statement: No retention window, TTL, legal-hold, tenant or identity provider semantics are declared by this contract. erasure_request_id names the request entity only; the policy that authorizes erasure is an owner decision and stays open as U-04.
open_owner_decisions.gate: Owner input U-04 (tenant model, identity provider, retention TTL matrix, legal-hold authority) recorded in docs/architecture/CP00_ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW.md section 11. It keeps ADR-0014 in proposed status. No numeric retention, TTL or legal-hold value may be declared by any lane before that input exists.

open_questions.question: What lease duration, heartbeat interval and grace window apply to an execution lease?
open_questions.gate: Decided by the jobs/operations slot no later than the first task that implements an execution lease (W4-JOB-01, durable stage state and bounded retry/resume, docs/stages/S04_core_audit_engine.md). No numeric value is chosen before that task and no lease implementation may proceed without it.

resolved_questions.question: Which canonical serialization defines the command payload fingerprint?
resolved_questions.resolution: The payload fingerprint is the sha256 digest of the RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme serialization of the schema-valid, default-normalized command payload. Transport headers and the idempotency key itself are excluded from the fingerprint input.
